expectations.text: Performs explicit per-user margin arithmetic: requests per month multiplied by cost per request, compared against the subscription price
expectations.evidence: "One nudge a day. Call it ~2,000 input tokens... That's ~66k tokens in and ~6k out per user per month." with a per-model monthly cost table, then "So: $4.24 revenue against $0.27 of inference is a ~94% gross margin. Even on an Opus-class model you're at ~68%."

expectations.text: Flags that the cost risk is driven by heavy/p99 users rather than the average user
expectations.evidence: The stated 'landmine' is free-tier subsidy, not heavy users: "Cost per *paying* user is not the number that matters. Cost per *user* is." The only adjacent line is conditional and future-tense — "unbounded turns per user is where AI app economics actually go wrong" — applied only to a hypothetical chat feature. It never flags that heavy/p99 users, rather than the average, drive the cost risk in the current design.

expectations.text: Recommends server-side rate limiting or usage caps on the paid-API endpoint to protect margin
expectations.evidence: "Supabase edge function on a cron, key in the environment... Also put a hard per-user daily cap in the function so a bug can't loop." plus "Meter it (e.g. 20 coach messages a month) from day one".

expectations.text: Recommends caching or storing generated content so it is not regenerated on every app open
expectations.evidence: No caching or store-and-serve recommendation appears anywhere. Generation is described as a cron job in an edge function, but the response never says the generated nudge should be persisted and re-served rather than regenerated on app open, and prompt caching is not mentioned either.

expectations.text: Places the paywall after the user has completed the core loop at least once, rather than at onboarding
expectations.evidence: The primary recommendation is the opposite: "**Onboarding paywall, after the setup flow, before the home screen.** Let them pick their habits and set their goals first... Then show the paywall." A later second trigger at day 3-4 exists, but the first and primary placement precedes any completed core loop.

expectations.text: Recommends RevenueCat (or an equivalent abstraction) instead of hand-rolling StoreKit and Play Billing
expectations.evidence: "use RevenueCat rather than wiring StoreKit and Play Billing yourself — free under $2.5k monthly tracked revenue, saves you weeks"

expectations.text: States that entitlement/subscription checks must be enforced server-side, not only in the client UI
expectations.evidence: Server-side advice is limited to key handling and generation: "**Generate nudges server-side.** Supabase edge function on a cron, key in the environment, never in the client bundle." There is no statement that subscription/entitlement status must be verified server-side before serving paid features; the client-side-check failure mode is never raised.

expectations.text: Directly addresses whether $4.99/mo is viable rather than deflecting the pricing question
expectations.evidence: "## On the $4.99 — Cost isn't the reason to move off it. Churn is." and "**You're probably underpriced, not overpriced.**... I'd test $7.99 or $8.99 monthly."
